newsitem.title: USA: US Q3 ECI shows labor costs not spurring inflation.
newsitem.headline: US Q3 ECI shows labor costs not spurring inflation.

text.p: The Employment Cost Index for the third quarter surprised economists by posting its smallest increase since the third quarter of 1995, suggesting labor costs are unlikely to spark a pickup in inflation.

"It's decidedly less than anyone had expected. This tells us there is no evidence that labor costs are creating an inflation threat," said David Resler, chief economist at Nomura Securities International Inc.
The Labor Department said the ECI rose by 0.6 percent in the third quarter, down from 0.8 percent in the second quarter.
The year-over-year ECI increase was 2.8 percent in the third quarter, compared to a 2.9 percent increase in the previous quarter.
Economists added an unusually small increase in the wage component of the ECI showed a tight labor market was still not generating significant inflationary pressures.
The wage component rose by 0.6 percent, the smallest quarterly gain since the third quarter of 1993, said Resler.
"Despite the low unemployment rate, wages are subdued. This means inflation won't (come) from the wage side," he added.

"Taken by itself in a vacuum, this number would lead people to say that the Federal Reserve will not move in December," noted Steve Ricchiuto, chief financial economist at Barclays de Zoete Wedd Government Securities Inc, addressing talk the Fed may raise interest rates in the future.
Ricchiuto noted the bond market reacted positively to the number, with the price of the benchmark 30-year Treasury rising just short of a full point soon after its release.
He cautioned, however, that the market would be looking at the non-farm payroll numbers due to be released on Friday as another indication of the state of the labor market.
